why: THE FACTORY'S OWN HEARTBEAT, declared so the rail can draw it and the pulse belt can read its stage length from it. The beat is the Windows task LivingFactory-Schedule running the factory's own engine/schedule.cjs - it came home from Telechurch's tools/factory on 2026-09-14, and the task's working directory (Telechurch) is now what makes Telechurch the primary subject; since 2026-09-14 that scheduler takes a subject (--root) and fans out one child tick per wired repo, this one included - so the same bell that rings Telechurch rings here, and the pulse card is written once per beat by the primary tick into .refer-factory/pulse-belt.jsonl. drivenBy rather than run because an external clock drives this and no scheduler may fire it as well; the child tick stamps this row and runs nothing for it. This replaces scripts/pulse-belt.trigger.json, whose account was true when written and false by the 14th: it said the engine could not be pointed here (it can now), that a Claude routine drove the beat (paused, superseded), and that nothing had ever ticked this repo (this declaration is what ends that).
